title: Gemini 4 Argon is now on LLM Gateway: here’s how it scores on voice tasks
summary: Gemini 4 Argon is live on AssemblyAI’s LLM Gateway. On the Voice Standard Bench it posts the top dictation score of 50+ models, but trails GPT-6 Luna on long transcripts at about 16× the cost per hour of audio.
body_markdown:
Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s newest model, is live on[LLM Gateway](https://www.assemblyai.com/products/llm-gateway) as of October 13, 2026. Call it with the model string` gemini-4-argon` and the same API key you use for speech-to-text.


We ran it through the[Voice Standard Bench](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/voice-standard-bench) : four voice tasks at four transcript lengths, the same run as every other model on the Gateway.


It has the top dictation score of any model we’ve tested. On the other three tasks, it scores within a few points of Gemini 3.8 Flash.

## What’s available on LLM Gateway


Gemini 4 Argon is served through Google Vertex, with US, EU, and global routing. Here’s what the[Models endpoint](https://www.assemblyai.com/products/llm-gateway/models) reports for it:


- **Model string:**` gemini-4-argon`
- **Context window:** 1,048,576 tokens, with up to 32,768 completion tokens
- **Parameters:**` tools` ,` tool_choice` ,` response_format` ,` stream` ,` max_tokens` , and` reasoning_effort` . There’s no` temperature` .
- **Price:** $2.00 per million prompt tokens and $10.00 per million completion tokens with global routing, at[provider rates with 0% markup](https://www.assemblyai.com/pricing) . In-region US or EU routing is 10% higher.


For comparison, Gemini 3.8 Flash lists at $0.75/$3.75 and GPT-6 Luna at $0.10/$0.50.


## How Gemini 4 Argon scores on the Voice Standard Bench


The Voice Standard Bench[scores each model on four tasks](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/voice-standard-bench-methodology) developers run on transcripts: dictation cleanup, information extraction, summarization, and text correction, on real transcripts from 30 seconds to an hour.1 We compare Gemini 4 Argon with Gemini 3.8 Flash, the previous Gemini Flash release; GPT-6 Luna, a low-cost model that scores near the top of the run; and[Qwen3.5 4B Fast](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/qwen-4b-llm-gateway) , the small open model AssemblyAI hosts for fast rewrite tasks.

Argon leads on dictation, stays within a few points of Gemini 3.8 Flash everywhere else, and trails GPT-6 Luna from 15 minutes up. Qwen3.5 4B Fast is the fastest and cheapest of the four at every length, but it’s built for short rewrites, and its scores drop sharply on longer transcripts.


[See Gemini 4 Argon against 50+ models on the Voice Standard Bench](https://www.assemblyai.com/voice-standard/tasks)


## Where it wins: dictation


Dictation is the task where a user speaks and expects clean, formatted text back: filler words removed, punctuation added,[self-corrections resolved](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/dictation-cleanup) . Gemini 4 Argon had a performance score of 100 on 30-second clips and 99 on 2-minute clips, a 99.5 mean and the highest performance score of the[50+ models on the bench](https://www.assemblyai.com/voice-standard/tasks) .

Mean of the 30-second and 2-minute clips. Axis runs from 95 to 100. The five highest scores, then the three lowest-cost models within four points of Argon.


The models just behind it cost far less. Gemma 4 31B, GPT-6 Luna, and GLM-5.3 Flash all cost less than a tenth of Argon per hour of audio. At high volume that’s a lot to pay for two or three points, but where a single wrong correction matters, such as medical or legal dictation, Argon is worth testing first. It’s quick too: a 2.0-second median response on 30-second clips, against 4.1 seconds for Gemini 3.8 Flash.


If you’d rather not wire up speech-to-text and a cleanup pass yourself, the[Dictation API](https://www.assemblyai.com/products/dictation-api) does both in one call: a spoken clip in, finished, formatted text out. Pass an` llm_instruction` when you need the output in a specific shape, such as a bulleted task list or a chat message.

## Which model to use


- **Highest dictation accuracy:** Gemini 4 Argon. It has the top score on the bench and a 2-second median on short clips.
- **Dictation at volume:** GPT-6 Luna or Gemma 4 31B, within four points of Argon for less than a tenth of the cost.
- **Summarization and extraction on long transcripts:** GPT-6 Luna. It scores higher than Argon at 15 minutes and an hour, at about a sixteenth of the cost.
- **Already on Gemini 3.8 Flash:** stay, unless you need responses about twice as fast and can pay 28–45% more on non-dictation tasks.


Results on your own prompts and transcripts can differ, and switching models on LLM Gateway means changing one string.


[Don’t take our word for it. Benchmark on your own audio with Voice Standard Bench’s open-source benchmark](https://github.com/AssemblyAI/voice-standard-bench)


## Get started


Gemini 4 Argon works like every other model on LLM Gateway: one[OpenAI-compatible endpoint](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/llm-gateway/quickstart) , your AssemblyAI API key, and the model string.


Request


```text
import   requests


API_KEY   =   "YOUR_API_KEY"


transcript   =   open  (  "call-transcript.txt"  ).  read  ()


response   =   requests  .  post  (
"https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1/chat/completions"  ,
headers  =  {  "Authorization"  :   API_KEY  ,   "Content-Type"  :   "application/json"  },
json  =  {
"model"  :   "gemini-4-argon"  ,
"max_tokens"  :   1000  ,
"messages"  :   [
{
"role"  :   "system"  ,
"content"  :   "Rewrite this dictation as clean, formatted text. "
"Drop filler words and resolve self-corrections "
"to the speaker's final intent."  ,
},
{  "role"  :   "user"  ,   "content"  :   transcript  },
],
},
)


print  (  response  .  json  ()[  "choices"  ][  0  ][  "message"  ][  "content"  ])
```


Before you switch, run your own prompt over your own transcript on all three models. This loop prints the time and token counts for each, so you can weigh the answers against what they cost:


Compare three models


```text
import   time
import   requests


API_KEY   =   "YOUR_API_KEY"
MODELS   =   [  "gemini-4-argon"  ,   "gemini-3.8-flash"  ,   "gpt-6-luna"  ]


transcript   =   open  (  "call-transcript.txt"  ).  read  ()


for   model   in   MODELS  :
start   =   time  .  perf_counter  ()
r   =   requests  .  post  (
"https://llm-gateway.assemblyai.com/v1/chat/completions"  ,
json  =  {
"model"  :   model  ,
"messages"  :   [
{  "role"  :   "system"  ,   "content"  :   "Summarize this call in five bullet points."  },
{  "role"  :   "user"  ,   "content"  :   transcript  },
],
},
)
elapsed   =   time  .  perf_counter  ()   -   start
usage   =   r  .  json  ()[  "usage"  ]
print  (  f  "  {  model  }  :   {  elapsed  :.1f  }  s, "
f  "  {  usage  [  '  prompt_tokens  '  ]  }   in /   {  usage  [  '  completion_tokens  '  ]  }   out"  )
print  (  r  .  json  ()[  "choices"  ][  0  ][  "message"  ][  "content"  ],   "  \n  "  )
```

## Frequently asked questions


Is Gemini 4 Argon available on AssemblyAI’s LLM Gateway?


Yes. Gemini 4 Argon is live on LLM Gateway as of October 13, 2026, under the model string gemini-4-argon. It’s served through Google Vertex in US, EU, and global regions, and you call it with the same AssemblyAI API key and OpenAI-compatible endpoint as every other model on the Gateway.


How much does Gemini 4 Argon cost on LLM Gateway?


Gemini 4 Argon costs $2.00 per million prompt tokens and $10.00 per million completion tokens with global routing, at provider rates with 0% markup. In-region US or EU routing is 10% higher. On the Voice Standard Bench that works out to about $0.07 per hour of audio averaged across the four voice tasks.


Is Gemini 4 Argon better than Gemini 3.8 Flash for voice tasks?


Only slightly, and not on every task. Gemini 4 Argon scores 87.2 overall against Gemini 3.8 Flash’s 85.8. It’s ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash on dictation, information extraction, and summarization, and behind it on text correction. GPT-6 Luna scores higher than both on extraction, summarization, and text correction. It costs the same per hour of audio on dictation and 28–45% more on the other three tasks, but its median response time is roughly half of Gemini 3.8 Flash’s on transcripts up to 15 minutes.


What is the best LLM for dictation cleanup?


On the Voice Standard Bench, Gemini 4 Argon has the highest dictation score of the 50+ models tested, at 99.5 across 30-second and 2-minute clips. If cost matters more than the last few points, Gemma 4 31B (97.0) and GPT-6 Luna (96.0) score within four points at less than a tenth of the cost per hour of audio.


Which model should I use for long transcripts like hour-long meetings?


For transcripts of 15 minutes or longer, GPT-6 Luna is the stronger pick in this comparison: it scores 87 at 15 minutes and 85 at one hour, against Gemini 4 Argon’s 82 and 79, at about a sixteenth of the cost per hour of audio. Gemini 4 Argon returns faster at those lengths, with a 10.9-second median at one hour against GPT-6 Luna’s 19.0 seconds.


Does Gemini 4 Argon support tool calling and structured output?


Yes. On LLM Gateway, Gemini 4 Argon supports tools, tool_choice, response_format, stream, max_tokens, and reasoning_effort, with a 1,048,576-token context window and up to 32,768 completion tokens. It doesn’t accept a temperature parameter.


## Methodology


1 Figures are from the Voice Standard Bench run published on LLM Gateway’s Models endpoint, read October 14, 2026, at each model’s default reasoning effort. Scores are 0 to 100. Task scores are the mean across the transcript lengths each task runs at; dictation runs on 30- second and 2-minute clips only, the other three tasks at 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 15 minutes, and one hour. Cost per hour of audio uses global routing, and the overall figure weights the four lengths equally. Response time is the median across every call at that length.
